title: Robot Chef Cooks Noodles in Just 90 Seconds
paragraphs: Restaurants in many countries are finding it hard to hire enough workers. Now, a Japanese company has developed a robot that can cook a bowl of noodles in about 90 seconds.

The robot is called STEAMA, and it was made by SoftBank Robotics. It uses steam at a very high temperature and pressure to cook frozen noodle dishes. According to the company, every bowl has the same texture, temperature and quality.
SoftBank Robotics showed STEAMA at the National Restaurant Association Show in Chicago in May 2026. It was the company's first time bringing its cooking robots to the United States.

The company also showed a second robot called FLAMA. This robot can do many kitchen jobs. It can handle ingredients, add seasoning, stir-fry food, put food on plates and clean up. FLAMA went on sale in Japan in April 2026. It works with recipe software, so restaurants can make the same dishes in many different locations.

Why are restaurants interested in these robots? Many restaurants have problems finding workers, and wages are rising. Staff also often leave their jobs. At the same time, customers want faster and more consistent service.

SoftBank Robotics hopes to sell the robots to restaurants, company cafeterias and food courts. The company says it wants to redesign the way kitchens work around robots, rather than just sell single machines. Tatsuhiko Hata, an executive at SoftBank Robotics, said the company was excited to bring the robots to the US.
However, the company has not said how much the robots will cost.
Other cooking robots are also appearing. In China, for example, some restaurants use robots to make noodles. One noodle shop in Shenzhen can serve a bowl in just 48 seconds.
